MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "City of Evil and Heartwork combine melody with intense guitar work, which feels like a natural continuation of my repeated In Flames listening.",
    "Burning Red fits the heavy grooves I wanted after Ten Thousand Fists, while Weathered connects with the melodic hard rock I enjoyed in One Day Remains.",
    "A Matter Of Life And Death appeals to my interest in ambitious arrangements after Tool, and Degradation Trip fits my appetite for darker, heavier rock."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Please Please Me points toward early pop rather than the heavy guitars and intensity I want right now.",
    "Into the Now and Blow Up Your Video share a broad rock connection with my listening, but traditional or bluesy hard rock is less compelling to me here than melodic metal and darker rock.",
    "Blackstar did not give me enough recognizable connection to my current interests to choose it; that uncertainty does not mean I would dislike its music."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in guitar music seems to have been treated too broadly, as though different kinds of rock would satisfy the same mood.",
    "The more accessible rock in my history seems to have carried too much weight when it led to choices without the heaviness or darker feeling I currently want."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Several In Flames albums in my history make the combination of melody and metal intensity a particularly strong clue to what interests me.",
    "My later choices of Ten Thousand Fists and 10.000 Days suggest that heavy grooves and more involved arrangements matter to my current listening.",
    "I need a clear musical connection before trying something unfamiliar; a title I cannot place is not enough on its own."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations understood my interest in heavy guitar music, but sometimes stretched that interest into rock choices that lack the melody, intensity, or darker mood I want now."
}
